title: HeaderDateTime fields: invariants documented but not enforced by constructor
description: HeaderDateTime in mime-tree/src/header_typed.rs has public fields (hour, minute, second, day, month, year) with documented value ranges (e.g. hour 0-23, minute 0-59). The struct has no #[non_exhaustive] and the fields are pub, so callers can create HeaderDateTime { hour: 99, ... } without any validation. What goes wrong: downstream code that pattern-matches on or serializes a HeaderDateTime can receive out-of-range values it never expected, causing incorrect behavior (e.g. a UI displaying '99:61'). The struct is currently an output type from parse(), so callers should not be constructing it. Adding #[non_exhaustive] prevents construction by callers; if it must remain constructible, a new() constructor that validates ranges and returns Result<Self, _> would enforce the invariants. File: mime-tree/src/header_typed.rs.
close_reason: HeaderDateTime field invariants are documented as parser-produced guarantees. Adding runtime validation to a public struct with pub fields would break callers who construct values directly. The #[non_exhaustive] attribute (added in this session) prevents external struct literal construction, which is the main risk vector.
